rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window while retaining early compounds and driving off strongly retained ones. The retention and resolution pattern will guide window trimming, slope changes, and temperature optimization.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the two crowded pairs respond to reduced slope. The initial last-peak time leaves room to improve resolution while likely keeping all peaks within 10 minutes.

The limiting pair improved substantially with a shallower gradient. Raising phi0 narrows the gradient window at the same duration, further reducing slope while advancing the late peak to preserve the under-10-minute finish.

Lengthen the gradient by two minutes to improve the sole unresolved pair, whose resolution responded strongly to duration in the scouting runs. The last peak is expected near 9.6 minutes, leaving a chance to reach full resolution without a time penalty.
Injection 4 reached the maximum possible CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a 5 °C increase to shorten elution while checking whether the limiting pair retains R ≥ 1.5.

The limiting pair converged sharply at 45 °C; a larger temperature increase may separate it again after an elution-order reversal. Test this selectivity change with a shorter gradient, retaining injection 4 as the established maximum-score method.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness to improve the new limiting pair at 55 °C while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes. Check that the recently separated middle pair also remains above R = 1.5.

Narrow the gradient slightly to obtain the small resolution gain still needed at 55 °C. The last peak should remain near 9 minutes, potentially matching the maximum CRF with faster elution than injection 4.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 8’s slope to seek earlier elution at the maximum CRF. Check whether the early peaks remain sufficiently retained and both close pairs retain baseline resolution.

The upward window shift harmed the limiting pair, so test a lower starting organic fraction with the shorter 14-minute gradient. This may restore full resolution while finishing earlier than injection 8; injection 8 remains the fastest verified maximum-score method.

Shorten injection 10’s gradient by two minutes to test whether full resolution can be retained with earlier elution. The 4–5 pair may approach the resolution threshold, while the 6–7 pair previously tolerated steeper gradients at 55 °C.

Reduce the gradient span to recover resolution of the limiting pair at the 12-minute duration. This slope lies between injections 10 and 11 and should give full resolution with the last peak slightly earlier than injection 10.

Use a slightly steeper slope than injection 12 to seek a shorter fully resolved separation, with the limiting resolutions expected near 1.5–1.6. The reduced endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, so all peaks should still elute during the gradient.

With the maximum CRF secured, explore a faster, hotter gradient that may separate the current limiting pair after an elution-order reversal. This tests a different selectivity regime rather than making further small changes near injection 13’s resolution threshold.

Test a higher starting organic fraction in the fast 60 °C regime to widen the apparently reversed limiting pair and advance the last peak. Monitor the neighboring pair and early peaks for resolution losses; injection 13 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method.

Test whether a steeper gradient further separates the reversed limiting pair at 60 °C while shortening elution. The adjacent pair at R = 1.62 is the main risk, so this run will establish whether the fast regime can retain sufficient resolution.

The fast 60 °C regime shows competing resolution losses, so explore lower-temperature selectivity instead. A 30 °C run may separate the crowded middle peaks in a different order while the moderate gradient keeps late retention manageable.

Return to the successful 55 °C regime and test whether a lower starting organic fraction improves the limiting pair enough to permit a steeper gradient. Monitor the other close middle pair, which may lose resolution as phi0 decreases.

Test a slightly steeper gradient than injection 18 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary at low starting organic fraction. The two close middle pairs have little margin, so retain injection 18 as the fastest verified maximum-score method if resolution falls below 1.5.

Preserve injection 18’s successful slope while ending the gradient sooner, just above the estimated last-peak elution fraction of 0.57. This should reproduce its maximum-score separation with a shorter programmed gradient and lower final organic fraction.

Test a modest temperature decrease from injection 1 to shift its crowded middle peaks without lengthening the gradient. This explores a potentially faster fully resolved separation, while injection 20 remains the verified maximum-score benchmark.

Return to the successful 55 °C region and slightly flatten injection 12’s gradient to seek a larger minimum-resolution margin while keeping all peaks below 10 minutes. The maximum CRF is already achieved; this tests a potentially more robust alternative.
